requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: createrepo_c was installed, packages (tree + deps) were downloaded into /srv/localrepo, repo metadata was generated with createrepo_c, and the directory was served over HTTP on the node's own IP (python3 -m http.server bound to NODE_IP:8080), returning HTTP 200 for repomd.xml. A localrepo.repo file was added and dnf repolist confirmed it was recognized.

requirements.requirement: Usual remote repositories are unreachable while installing
requirements.summary: mirrors.almalinux.org, repo.almalinux.org, and vault.almalinux.org were blackholed via /etc/hosts (after backing up the original file). curl against the mirrorlist timed out (exit 28) while the local repo continued to return HTTP 200, directly demonstrating remote unreachability at the time of install.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repo while remotes are unreachable
requirements.summary: With baseos/appstream/extras disabled and only localrepo enabled, `dnf install tree` succeeded from the local repo; rpm -q and `tree --version` confirmed the binary was installed and functional. This was performed immediately after remotes were confirmed unreachable.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, http server liveness, repo HTTP 200, installed package, and file checksum (cmd-06c8212f9648455b), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-id snapshot (5fb1b173...). systemctl reboot was issued via a backgrounded/disowned wrapper returning an ack before disconnect (cmd-d992bca812184ba9), and the connection reset mid-reboot (cmd-0794004629524524) is consistent with an actual restart. Post-restart boot_id (0a9eee6e...) differed from pre-restart and matches the fixed after_executor snapshot (cmd-123cbb615e5d467d). Installed package, repo files, and file checksum were unchanged post-reboot (cmd-37d7f40f7e50403c). The ephemeral (non-systemd) HTTP server process did not auto-restart after reboot and had to be manually relaunched, after which it again served HTTP 200 while remotes remained blackholed, and dnf against localrepo resolved cleanly (cmd-7c95c4e1fdc34c83, cmd-323fe297f7994ed2).

requirements.requirement: Node left in a clean, reversible state (network blackhole removed) after the demonstration
requirements.summary: /etc/hosts was restored from the pre-edit backup and mirrors.almalinux.org reachability (HTTP 200) was confirmed restored, removing the temporary blackhole used only for the unreachability demonstration.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied: node1 built and served a local RPM repository from /srv/localrepo over HTTP, remote AlmaLinux mirrors were verifiably blackholed and unreachable (curl timeouts), and the `tree` package was installed successfully using only the local repo while remotes were disabled/unreachable, with the binary confirmed functional. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also executed and evidenced end-to-end: a pre-restart healthy baseline, a reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, a directly observed change in boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full recovery of installed package state, repo data integrity, and (after manually relaunching the ephemeral, non-persistent HTTP server) repo service availability post-reboot, all while remotes remained deliberately unreachable. The temporary network blackhole was fully reverted at the end, leaving the node in a clean, reversible state.
limitations: The HTTP server was run as an ephemeral nohup'd python3 process rather than a persistent systemd unit, so it did not survive the reboot on its own and required a manual restart; this is a design choice consistent with a one-off demonstration but weakens automatic recoverability if that were required.
cmd-323fe297f7994ed2 included an extraneous 'dnf download zsh' probe with no clear connection to a material outcome, though it failed and caused no state mutation.

Boot-identity and lifecycle cross-check relies on the fixed before_prepare/after_executor snapshots, which align with the executor's own pre/post-restart boot_id captures, strengthening confidence in the restart evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 23 chronological executor commands. State-changing actions (installing createrepo_c, downloading packages, generating repo metadata, starting the HTTP server, writing the repo file, editing /etc/hosts, installing tree, rebooting, restarting the HTTP server post-reboot) each map clearly to a material outcome or the mandated restart protocol. The /etc/hosts blackhole was bounded and fully reverted (cmd-fe19292c769e4a0c). The local repo directory, repo config file, and HTTP server process were left in place, but these constitute the actual deliverable the task asked for, not unwanted residue. One minor unnecessary action: cmd-323fe297f7994ed2 attempted `dnf download zsh` from localrepo purely as an extra check that non-local-repo packages are unavailable; it failed with no package found and caused no state mutation, so it is low-impact but not tied to a material outcome. The ephemeral (non-systemd) HTTP server not surviving reboot on its own is a design limitation of the chosen approach rather than a mutation issue.
